chunks: Abu Ayyub narrated from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
"The one performing i'tikaf must not smell perfume, take pleasure in fragrant plants, engage in disputation, buy, or sell."

He said: "Whoever performs i'tikaf for three days has the choice on the fourth day: if he wishes, he may add another three; and if he wishes, he may leave the mosque. But if he remains for two days after the three, then he must not leave the mosque until he completes another three days."

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque in which i'tikaf is observed
key_terms.الْمُعْتَكِفُ: the person observing i'tikaf in the mosque
key_terms.بِالرَّيْحَانِ: with fragrant plants or aromatic herbs

ai.seo_question: What is prohibited during i'tikaf, and when does continuing i'tikaf become binding?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for i'tikaf, forbidding the retreatant from perfume, fragrant enjoyment, disputation, buying, and selling during the retreat. It also explains the binding duration: after completing three days, one may either leave or continue, but remaining two additional days makes completion of a further three days obligatory.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2097 - It is narrated by Abu Ayyub, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (as), who said:
"The one performing i'tikaf must not smell perfume, enjoy fragrant plants, engage in argumentation, buy, or sell."

Imam (as) further said: "Whoever performs i'tikaf for three days has the option on the fourth day: if they wish, they may continue for another three days, or if they wish, they may leave the mosque. However, if they stay for two days after the initial three, they must complete another three days and not leave the mosque until they have done so."
